learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how coding automates biological research, and discover how Systems Biology studies the entire cell as one giant, interconnected network!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Biologists write code (usually in Python, R, or Perl) to automate repetitive tasks, parse massive DNA files, and perform complex statistical analyses on biological datasets.

Reductionism breaks a cell down to study individual parts (like one gene). Systems biology looks at the whole picture—how thousands of genes, proteins, and metabolites interact together as a complex system.
Visualizing biological systems as webs. Genes or proteins are 'nodes' (dots), and their interactions are 'edges' (lines). Examples include Metabolic networks and Gene Regulatory networks.
Using math and computer code to build a digital model of a cell or organ. Scientists can simulate how the cell reacts to a drug or a disease digitally before testing a real living subject.

The ultimate application of systems biology. Instead of just understanding natural networks, scientists design and build entirely new biological parts, devices, and systems that do not exist in the natural world.

fun_activity.title: 🌐 Draw Your Network
fun_activity.instructions: Draw 5 dots (Nodes) representing: You, your Mom, your Dad, your best friend, and your teacher. Draw lines (Edges) between the people who talk to each other. You just created a basic social network, exactly how systems biology maps proteins!

exam_tips: 📌 Systems biology requires a multi-disciplinary approach: it combines biology, computer science, mathematics, and physics.
📌 Python and R are the most popular programming languages in biotechnology today due to their powerful libraries for data analysis.
📌 Be able to define 'emergence' or 'emergent properties'—features of a complex system that individual parts do not possess on their own (e.g., a beating heart vs. single heart cells).
quick_recap: ⭐ The mantra of Systems Biology is 'the whole is greater than the sum of its parts'.
⭐ Automation via programming is necessary because modern DNA sequencers generate terabytes of data daily.
⭐ Synthetic biology treats DNA like computer code that can be written to program cells to produce biofuels or medicines.
